commentary.seminaVerbi: Paul’s jab at “bewitchment” lands close to Plato’s worry about doxa: the mind can be spellbound by inherited forms and mistake compliance for truth. The pivot is not moral effort but a different mode of knowing, nearer to the Upanishadic contrast between ritual performance and direct insight into what is given (speculation). Luke’s midnight knocking rhymes with Zen’s “great doubt” and relentless koan-pressure: the door yields not to merit but to sustained, naked need. The father who gives good gifts echoes the Bhagavad Gita’s assurance that what is sincerely sought is met, not always as requested but as fitting; and the Sufi insistence that persistence in asking is itself a polishing of desire until it can receive (speculation). The “Spirit” as the gift behind gifts parallels prana/ruach as animating breath across traditions, an inward endowment rather than an external wage.
commentary.excursus:
Paul’s insult is a diagnosis: they’ve traded the raw risk of being seized by something beyond them for the narcotic of technique. “Works of the law” isn’t morality; it’s control, the fantasy that the self can finish what the Spirit began. “Who hath bewitched you” lands like shame because it names a desire they won’t admit: they want the crucified Christ as an image they can manage, not a wound that keeps opening.

Luke’s midnight scene makes the same point without piety. Prayer is not polite; it is pressure. The door is shut, the house is dark, the friend is irritated, and the asker is desperate enough to keep knocking until love looks like coercion. The gift comes not because the one inside is kind, but because refusal becomes unbearable.

So “ask, seek, knock” is not a promise of serenity but a permission to be relentless. Even the comparison with fathers is edged: “you, being evil,” still feed your children; goodness here is not purity but instinct. The Spirit is given the way bread is given at midnight—because hunger will not be argued with, and because the only faith that survives is the one that keeps making a nuisance of itself.
commentary.synthesis: God grants the Spirit by faith’s reception, not by legal performance, and he ordains persistent asking as the creaturely mode of that reception. To seek perfection by flesh is to deny both the cross’s disclosure and the Father’s pledged generosity.

gospel.text: The parable is not about persuading a reluctant God but about training desire into speech and motion: ask/seek/knock names a sustained posture, not a single request. The universality (“every one”) frames prayer as a rule of the kingdom rather than an exception for the devout.

Jesus argues from lesser to greater: even compromised human fatherhood tends toward fitting gifts; divine fatherhood cannot be outdone by its own shadow. The climactic gift is not relief but the “good Spirit,” making prayer the appointed means by which God gives God.

reading.text: Paul prosecutes a category mistake: treating the Spirit as a wage paid by legal performance. The cross was “set forth” as the definitive disclosure of God’s action; therefore the community’s present experience of Spirit and power must be interpreted as divine initiative rather than human leverage.

The argument turns on temporal logic: beginning and completion must belong to the same principle. To switch from Spirit to flesh is to change the kind of story their lives are—turning endurance into wasted expenditure unless they reattach it to the original promise.

marginalia.text: “Bewitched”: error as enchantment, not mere mistake; the crucified is public, not private.
Two economies posed as a single question: law-works versus faith-hearing; reception, not achievement.
Perfection by “flesh” is regression disguised as progress; the finish line becomes a treadmill.
Suffering becomes evidence only if it has an object; “if it be yet in vain” leaves a crack for return.
Miracles as audit trail: the giver’s method exposes the recipient’s theory.
Midnight prayer: need arrives at the wrong hour; dependence is inconvenient by nature.
The closed door is not denial but resistance; domestic order set against sudden charity.
Importunity wins without intimacy; persistence substitutes for merit.
Stone/serpent: the terror of misrecognition—gift turned counterfeit.
“Being evil” is baseline anthropology; the comparison shames doubt and elevates the Father’s giving.

hoursOfPrayer.prayer: Almighty and eternal God, who in your generous love surpass the merits and desires of those who implore you, pour out your mercy upon us, that you may free our conscience from every anxiety and grant us even what we do not dare to ask. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God for ever and ever.
hoursOfPrayer.label: Matins

hoursOfPrayer.prayer: Almighty and eternal God: enlighten with your light the peoples who live in darkness and in the shadow of death, for by that light the Dayspring from on high has visited us, Jesus Christ our Lord. Who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God for ever and ever.
hoursOfPrayer.label: Lauds

hoursOfPrayer.prayer: Lord, you who at the hour of Terce sent the Holy Spirit upon the apostles gathered in prayer, grant that we too may share in the gifts of this Spirit. Through Jesus Christ our Lord.
hoursOfPrayer.label: Terce

hoursOfPrayer.prayer: Almighty and eternal God, before you there is neither darkness nor gloom; therefore let the brightness of your light shine upon us, so that, keeping your commandments, we may walk faithfully in your ways with hearts enlarged. Through Jesus Christ our Lord.
hoursOfPrayer.label: Sext

hoursOfPrayer.prayer: Look upon your family at prayer, Lord, and grant that, imitating the examples of patience of your Son, it may never falter in adversity. Through Jesus Christ our Lord.
hoursOfPrayer.label: Nones

hoursOfPrayer.prayer: Almighty God, we give you thanks for the day now ending and implore your mercy, that you may graciously forgive us all the faults which, through the frailty of the human condition, we have committed this day. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God for ever and ever.
hoursOfPrayer.label: Vespers

hoursOfPrayer.prayer:
Let us pray:
Lord our God, grant us a peaceful rest that restores our strength, now worn down by the day’s work; so that, strengthened by your help, we may always serve you with our whole body and spirit. Through Jesus Christ our Lord.
hoursOfPrayer.label: Compline

lines: O senseless Galatians, who hath bewitched you that you should not obey the truth: before whose eyes Jesus Christ hath been set forth, crucified among you?
This only would I learn of you: Did you receive the Spirit by the works of the law or by the hearing of faith?
Are you so foolish that, whereas you began in the Spirit, you would now be made perfect by the flesh?
Have you suffered so great things in vain? If it be yet in vain.
He therefore who giveth to you the Spirit and worketh miracles among you: doth he do it by the works of the law or by the hearing of the faith?
readings.heading: A reading from the Letter of St. Paul to the Galatians

lines: And he said to them: Which of you shall have a friend and shall go to him at midnight and shall say to him: Friend, lend me three loaves,
Because a friend of mine is come off his journey to me and I have not what to set before him.
And he from within should answer and say: Trouble me not; the door is now shut, and my children are with me in bed. I cannot rise and give thee.
Yet if he shall continue knocking, I say to you, although he will not rise and give him because he is his friend; yet, because of his importunity, he will rise and give him as many as he needeth.
And I say to you: Ask, and it shall be given you: seek, and you shall find: knock, and it shall be opened to you.
For every one that asketh receiveth: and he that seeketh findeth: and to him that knocketh it shall be opened:
And which of you, if he ask his father bread, will he give him a stone? Or a fish, will he for a fish give him a serpent?
Or if he shall ask an egg, will he reach him a scorpion?
If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father from heaven give the good Spirit to them that ask him?
